newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Overseas to power Blue Circle.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Overseas to power Blue Circle.

text.p: Continued strength in the U.S. and rapid growth in the Chile and Malaysia construction markets will help UK building materials group Blue Circle Industries Plc deliver a strong set of results next Tuesday, analysts said.
Blue Circle, Britain's biggest cement producer, is predicted to reveal pretax profit of between 90.0 and 116.5 million stg, up from 104.1 million stg a year before.
A strong balance sheet will also help deliver a healthy first-half dividend increase, with median expectations for a payout of 4.25 pence compared with 4.00 in 1995.
UBS analyst Simon Brown said the results will reflect the improved picture in the U.S. construction market "which has continued this year both in volumes and prices in terms in cement."
The group said in March it anticipates strong growth at its Malaysia and Chile units in 1996. "It is the overseas' side that is driving it ahead," Brown added.

Analysts will be watching the results for further details on Blue Circle's plans to restructure its UK cement operations, announced in June, as it strives to become Europe's most cost-efficient producer.

There are also hopes that cost savings from Blue Circle's reorganisation of its European heating operations may flow through earlier than originally expected. UBS's Brown said the restructuring, which the company expects to result in annual savings of 25 million stg, "seem to be going well."
But Panmure Gordon's Robin Hardy injected a note of caution, questioning Blue Circle's ability to deliver all it has promised.
"People have accepted they will achieve this without any problems," said Hardy, adding that Blue Circle has a history of "not quite getting it right" on heating.

Hardy also expressed concerns about the vulnerability of earnings in fast-growing and isolated Chile, where profit margins last year exceeded 30 percent, if other producers decided to start shipping in cement.

Questions may also be raised about Blue Circle's ability to slash fuel costs at its cement kilns by switching to combustible chemicals following a judicial challenge to rival Redland Plc on environmental grounds.
